## TL;DR

Task #1057 fixes two lifecycle bugs: the Work board card must not read PAUSED while a server handoff is still running, and a handoff deferred for unread queued messages must auto-resume the engineer instead of sitting idle. Review pass 2 asked to scope the deferred-handoff retry counter to one deferral episode and to remove a duplicate `statusLine` prop in `ChecksProgressDisplay.vue`. Both are addressed, along with table-driven regression tests. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passes after formatting `agents.ts`.

## Work and rationale

The incidents on 2026-11-08 showed the card trusting “is an engineer process running” even when the control plane was still executing handoff steps (check, verify, review, capture). Operators saw PAUSED with Restart work while remote validation and shot capture were active. Separately, when an engineer ended a turn with a driver message still queued, handoff correctly deferred but nothing relaunched the engineer, so tasks sat until manual `repoos start`.

The UI side centralizes active-task labeling in `task-card-status.ts` and the repo store’s `handoffInFlight` helper. While that signal is true, `TaskCard.vue` and pipeline siblings show the running-checks presentation and suppress Pause/Restart, matching the server’s handoff status stream rather than the agent runner’s live entry.

The server side already recorded deferrals and scheduled a microtask resume after turn cleanup, persisting `deferred_handoff_resume_count` in task extra with cap `MAX_DEFERRED_HANDOFF_RESUMES` (2). Review pass 2 correctly noted the counter only incremented: after two deferrals in separate sessions, a third deferral would never auto-resume even though blocking messages had long been delivered. The fix hooks `maybeClearDeferredHandoffResumeCount` into the queue-delivery callback invoked once blocking human messages are delivered, deleting the extra field when no blocking messages remain. That preserves the per-episode loop bound without permanently exhausting the budget.

## Approaches tried

Earlier rounds implemented the card signal and auto-resume path; this session focused on review findings and gate hygiene. I confirmed the duplicate `statusLine` entries at review tree `2333ca1d3` were already removed on HEAD—props and `cardLine` each reference `statusLine` once. I added no redundant UI refactors.

For the retry budget, clearing on message delivery matches the mental model “one deferral episode” rather than a lifetime task counter. Alternatives (timestamp-scoped keys or tying reset to handoff status clear) were heavier and harder to test; delivery is the observable moment operators care about.

## Challenges and blockers

A prior turn timed out before handoff. Review pass 2 also flagged possible merge conflicts in `ChecksProgressDisplay.vue` and `PipelineCard.vue`; `git merge-tree` against current main reports a clean merge for this branch.

Scoped `repoos check` first hung in remote validation’s test stream; a subsequent run passed remote gates but failed `check-fmt:check` on `agents.ts` until `bun run fmt`. Earlier handoff failure citing browser capture timeout was environmental, not a product regression on this diff.

## Key learnings

Handoff finalization is server-owned state that can outlive the engineer process; the card must follow `handoffInFlight`, not runner liveness alone. Deferred handoff with queued human input is intentional back-pressure, but once the engineer has exited with no entry, recovery must be explicit and bounded. Persisting retry counts without resetting on “messages read” confuses episode caps with lifetime caps and recreates the idle-deferral failure mode reviewers predicted.
